target_statement: Determine the order of the largest group G_4 generated by four involutions and satisfying (xy)^4=1 for every pair of involutions x,y in G_4.

source_clauses.text: For a positive integer m, let G_m be the largest group generated by m involutions such that (xy)^4=1 for any two involutions x,y in G_m.
What is the order of G_4?
It is known that the order of G_3 is 2^11. Also cf. 18.58.

constraints.statement: G_4 is generated by four involutions; each of the four specified generators has order exactly 2.
For every pair x,y that are involutions anywhere in G_4, not merely for pairs of the four chosen generators, (xy)^4=1.
The target is the largest/universal group in this class, so a quotient or one finite example is not automatically G_4.
Determine |G_4| exactly, including proving finiteness if a finite integer is claimed.

excluded_scopes: Groups imposing (xy)^4=1 only on pairs of chosen generators
A finite quotient not proved equal to the universal G_4

success_criteria.proof: Determine |G_4| exactly and prove that the computed/presented object has the required universal property.
success_criteria.counterexample: If the presupposed finite order fails, prove the universal object infinite or prove that no largest object exists under the source definition.
partial_progress: A certified finite quotient/lower bound together with a clear statement that it is not yet the universal group.
A proved structural or nilpotency reduction applying to every four-generated group in the class.
success_criteria.certificate: A checkable confluent presentation, p-quotient/collection certificate plus a universality proof, or a rigorous infinitude certificate.

truth_likelihood.rationale: Here 'truth' means that the intended universal object is finite and has a determinable order; the m=3 context favors finiteness but does not settle m=4.

priority.rationale: The exact target is important and certificate-shaped, but universal-property verification is substantially harder than finding a quotient.
